title: Resilience & Escalation Sprint Review with Halo Fintech
summary: Discovery-style security review focused on incident response, BCDR targets (RTO/RPO), escalation paths and how Redwood's Dedicated/Private options support Halo's residency+KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 pack, run a tabletop with Halo ops, provide KMS BYOK design sketch, and propose SLA language for critical inference endpoints.
topics: SOC 2 / ISO evidence and audit reports
BCDR: RTO / RPO targets & backup cadence
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 Type II report and PCA controls matrix (Lena) by 2026-09-06
Schedule full tabletop run (ops + infra) for week of 2026-09-20 (Samir to propose slots)
Share BYOK/KMS architecture sketch and HSM options (Iris) by 2026-09-08
Draft proposed SLA excerpt for critical inference endpoints (Lena) by 2026-09-10
Customer to share network diagram and expected egress IPs for VPC peering (Halo) by 2026-09-07
action_items: Lena Moreno: Send SOC2 Type II and controls mapping — due 2026-09-06
Samir Patel: Arrange tabletop dates and invite Halo ops — due 2026-09-09
Iris Chen: Produce BYOK/HSM design sketch + short risks doc — due 2026-09-08

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-02 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~48m | Recording: auto
Attendees: Lena Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Iris Chen (Redwood Security PM); Daniel Ruiz (CISO, Halo), Maya Okoye (Head of Platform), Tom Hsu (SRE), Priya Narang (Compliance), Alexei Morozov (Infra)

Summary: quick alignment on security/compliance requirements and incident/BCDR expectations. Focused on RTO/RPO for inference endpoints, BYOK/KMS options, EU data residency constraints, RBAC/SSO provisioning, and runbook/escalation flow.

00:00:12 - Lena (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can start — goal for today is to walk through your resilience questions and make sure our proposed Dedicated/Private patterns line up with Halo's ops and compliance needs.
00:00:28 - Daniel (Halo - CISO): sounds good, quick context — we're evaluating a vendor for low-latency inference, but we're strict on data residency and customer-controlled keys. also we need a clear BCDR plan, that's the gating item for legal.
00:00:45 - Lena: totally, and just to confirm — you want EU-only hosting for the model/data, BYOK and HSM-backed key management, SOC2 evidence, plus RTO/RPO targets for production endpoints?
00:01:00 - Daniel: yes, precisely. RTO and RPO are the ones we want to validate — our SRE asked for sub-15 minute RTO for critical endpoints and RPO <= 5 minutes for stateful caches.
00:01:18 - Samir (SE): okay, good, that's realistic to discuss. quick disclaimer, depending on Dedicated vs Private we have different knobs — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in our cloud region, Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full control over network and KMS.
00:01:34 - Maya (Halo): can you clarify the difference on KMS? we need BYOK — ideally we hold key material in our own HSM but still let Redwood serve the model.
00:01:48 - Iris (Redwood Security PM): yes, BYOK is supported for Private deployments — we can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM via standard KMIP or cloud KMS APIs. for Dedicated (Redwood-managed infra) we offer a managed KMS option but with BYOK via customer-managed keys in the cloud provider (e.g., AWS KMS with key policy restricting Redwood).
00:02:10 - Tom (SRE): do you have an example flow and what the key lifecycle looks like? rotation, revocation, how long you keep logs about key usage?
00:02:22 - Iris: we'll share a sketch but short answer: key rotation is customer-driven for BYOK; Redwood logs key usage with request-level metadata into audit logs; log retention policy can be extended — default is 90 days but we can support 12 months with enterprise retention add-on.
00:02:40 - Priya (Compliance): 12 months is our minimum for audit, ideally 13 months to match our archive cycle. also we need proof that logs are tamper-evident.
00:02:52 - Iris: understood — tamper-evident append-only logs and delivery to your SIEM (we support Splunk/Datadog/ELK) are standard for Private installs; for Dedicated we can push signed log bundles or integrate with your SIEM via secure forwarders.
00:03:10 - Daniel: for SOC2, do you already have the Type II? we'll need the report and the PCA matrix mapping controls to your processes.
00:03:22 - Lena: yes we have SOC2 Type II; I will send the report and a high-level controls mapping (what they test). we also have ISO evidence for our infra controls.
00:03:36 - Alexei (Infra): on network — we'll want to peer into an EU region, and make sure outbound IPs are pinned so our firewall rules can allow calls. what does that look like on Dedicated?
00:03:49 - Samir: Dedicated endpoints can be pinned to Egress IP sets per region; Private with VPC peering gives you direct internal networking and no public egress as long as you configure it. We'll document the egress IP ranges and NAT behavior.
00:04:06 - Maya: okay good. now on BCDR — we run a rotated on-call and need a clear escalation path. what does your SRE on-call look like, and what are your RTO/RPO commitments in writing?
00:04:22 - Samir: operationally, Redwood has a tiered escalation: on-call engineer -> escalation to infra SRE lead -> platform on-call -> engineering manager and then exec on-call if needed. for SLA we typically offer 99.95% for Dedicated critical endpoints and 99.9% for hosted tiers; we can propose contractual language for 99.95 with error budgets and credits.
00:04:46 - Daniel: 99.95 is acceptable, but we need measurable RTO for incident runs — e.g., for P1 we expect a mitigation window of 15 minutes to restore degraded service or failover. can you support automated fallback to a warm model variant in another region?
00:05:03 - Samir: yes, smart routing supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants in other regions or lower-capacity pools. for Private installs, customer-managed failover is typical but we can operate failover via our control plane if agreed in the runbook.
00:05:18 - Tom: what's the usual RPO for your KV/cache state? our session tokens and KV cache are critical — if you lose the KV we want RPO as close to zero as possible.
00:05:30 - Samir: continuous prefix/KV caching introduces statefulness — for Dedicated we replicate KV across availability zones with async replication. RPO depends on replication window; we can target sub-1 minute RPO with aggressive replication and WAL shipping. that has cost trade-offs.
00:05:50 - Daniel: cost trade-offs are expected, we want the design and the numbers so legal can sign off.
00:05:58 - Lena: we'll draft a few architectures and cost delta scenarios in the BYOK doc.
00:06:08 - 00:06:30 - [crosstalk] — brief sidebar about schedule options for tabletop, everyone confirms weeks.
00:06:45 - Priya: on RBAC and SSO — we need SCIM provisioning and ability to map our roles to Redwood roles (admin, ops, read-only). also MFA enforcement via SAML.
00:06:58 - Iris: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based with customizable role bindings; we can add constraint rules for resource-level access. MFA enforcement is upstream via IdP.
00:07:14 - Alexei: any audit of role changes? we require a changelog for user/role modifications for 13 months.
00:07:24 - Iris: yes, role changes are logged with actor, timestamp, IP and old/new state. retention configurable; can export to your SIEM.
00:07:36 - Maya: great. a question on incident notifications: we need integration with PagerDuty and a phone escalation path for sev1. how does that map today?
00:07:49 - Samir: we push alerts to PagerDuty and can configure runbook hooks. phone escalation is available for enterprise customers as a paged escalation; we can include a primary SRE on-call list in the runbook and automatic escalation intervals (e.g., 5m -> 10m -> 30m).
00:08:05 - Daniel: good. also how do you handle post-mortems and root-cause evidence for regulator reviews?
00:08:16 - Iris: post-mortems live in our incident tracker; we can provide redacted timelines and logs relevant to the incident. we keep evidence for X months — default 6 months — but again retention can be extended with the enterprise evidence pack.
00:08:30 - Tom: what's X? can you be specific on evidence retention tied to a contract?
00:08:36 - Iris: yes — evidence retention commitments would be contractually specified; typical enterprise add-on is 12-24 months.
00:08:45 - Lena: quick note — customers on Private mode often choose 24-month retention for auditability.
00:08:52 - 00:09:10 - [Pause] short audio glitch, partial overlap.
00:09:22 - Daniel: can you walk through an example incident run? say database connectivity in EU region fails, what's the sequence to failover and notify Halo?
00:09:34 - Samir: step 1 auto-detect via health checks and telemetry; step 2 if below threshold we attempt local recovery (restart processes); step 3 if recovery fails within the configured window (e.g., 5m) we trigger routing to warm standby region or model variant; step 4 we create P1 incident ticket, notify via PagerDuty and email, and run the escalation tree. each step is logged and available in the incident timeline for post-mortem.
00:09:58 - Maya: important — we want the ability to control failover thresholds; sometimes legal requires us to opt into or out of cross-border failover.
00:10:09 - Iris: that's possible — we can configure routing policies to require explicit approval for cross-region failover for your account. we'll include that in the runbook template.
00:10:22 - Priya: another compliance question: do you support data deletion/verifiable purge if we request deletion for specific datasets?
00:10:32 - Lena: yes, data lifecycle APIs allow deletion requests; for Private deployments, you control the storage and can verify deletion. for Dedicated/hosted we provide verifiable deletion logs and certificates upon request.
00:10:45 - Daniel: and replication — if data copied into backups or caches exist in other zones, how's purge handled?
00:10:54 - Samir: purge hooks can cascade to caches and backups; for backups we maintain snapshot deletion metadata and can certify deletion after retention window elapses. we will detail the guarantee and exceptions (e.g., immutable logs for legal holds).
00:11:12 - Alexei: about SLA credits, can you share sample language? we need SLO definitions, measurement windows, and remediation credits.
00:11:23 - Lena: yes — we'll attach sample SLA clauses. typical is 99.95% monthly uptime with credits scaled based on outage minutes beyond threshold. we also specify measurement (client-facing endpoints only) and exclude scheduled maintenance windows with notice.
00:11:42 - Daniel: okay, good. question on tests — how often do you run DR tests and can Halo join?
00:11:50 - Samir: we run annual full DR drills and quarterly tabletop exercises; customers can join or request dedicated drills — for Private we can run dedicated drills in your environment.
00:12:02 - Priya: we'd like quarterly table-top with our ops and legal present for the first year.
00:12:08 - Lena: we will plan that into the onboarding runbook.
00:12:14 - 00:12:30 - [brief aside about sample audit checklist Lena will send]
00:12:45 - Daniel: small nit — our compliance team will need signed BAA and data processing addendum; can you confirm Redwood supports standard DPA + BAA?
00:12:56 - Lena: yes we have standard DPA and BAA templates; legal can review changes. I'll include them in the package.
00:13:05 - Maya: circling back to KMS — what's the attestation/crypto boundary for Redwood-managed keys vs customer-managed?
00:13:15 - Iris: Redwood-managed keys keep key material in our managed HSMs; with BYOK, key material never leaves customer KMS/HSM. we only get wrapped keys or use envelope encryption — we can detail trust flow in the architecture sketch.
00:13:30 - Tom: do you support on-prem HSMs talking over KMIP?
00:13:34 - Iris: yes, for Private installs we support KMIP and HSM integration; we've implemented with Thales and AWS CloudHSM patterns.
00:13:44 - 00:14:05 - [short pause while someone checks chat link]
00:14:16 - Samir: one more operational detail — when we talk about backups, we usually snapshot model artifacts and config daily and store across AZs; hot KV is replicated more frequently. we can alter cadence depending on RPO needs.
00:14:31 - Alexei: and retention for backups? regulatory often asks 7 years for financial logs — is that possible?
00:14:40 - Iris: yes, long-term retention is available via archive tiers; cost and retrieval latency are trade-offs we'll include in the proposal.
00:14:51 - Daniel: if we require on-prem, what's the support model? do you do remote ops or do we run it entirely?
00:14:59 - Samir: on-prem option can be delivered either as customer-run with operator docs or as a managed private deployment where Redwood provides ops under an enterprise support agreement. we do both.
00:15:12 - Maya: would managed mean Redwood has network access into our environment? that's a legal point.
00:15:20 - Lena: managed means we have specific, limited operator access flows over mutually agreed channels; everything is logged and subject to your approval. we can provide jump-host access, ephemeral credentials, or a bastion approach as per your security policy.
00:15:34 - Priya: please capture that detail — legal will want to see scope of access.
00:15:39 - Lena: noted.
00:15:45 - 00:16:05 - [silence while Iris prepares BYOK slide link in chat]
00:16:08 - Iris: I'm posting the BYOK/KMS options doc link in the chat — it's a high-level primer, the sketch we'll send will have more detail.
00:16:18 - Daniel: thanks. minor transcription — when you say "warm standby" do you mean kept-up replica with served traffic suppressed, or just a model artifact ready to spin up?
00:16:29 - Samir: warmed standby can be either — we offer cold (artifact only), warm (loaded model, idle), and hot (actively serving in another AZ). warm is typical for cost vs latency balance.
00:16:43 - Tom: do you have metrics on failover time for warm standby?
00:16:48 - Samir: for warm standby we usually see failover in 30s-2m depending on checkpoint loading and KV sync; hot is essentially instant routing. we'll put measured numbers from our benchmarks in the runbook.
00:17:03 - Maya: please include test evidence — we will need benchmark CSVs showing failover latencies.
00:17:10 - Lena: will do.
00:17:18 - 00:17:36 - [discussion about scheduling tabletop slots]
00:17:40 - Daniel: final compliance question — are you able to sign mutual NDAs and provide a shared evidence room for auditors?
00:17:49 - Lena: yes — we use a secure evidence room for customers during audits and sign MNDA/NDAs; we'll include onboarding steps for audit access.
00:17:58 - Priya: perfect. one more thing — SIEM integration, we'll want ability to forward all request-level logs and role-change events. can Redwood provide a sustained log stream and not just bundles?
00:18:10 - Samir: yes, we can provide streaming via secure forwarder to Splunk/Datadog/ELK with TLS and client auth. the volume/throughput has costs; we'll provide estimates.
00:18:22 - Alexei: about encryption in transit — TLS mutual auth for private peering?
00:18:28 - Iris: TLS 1.2/1.3 enforced. for VPC peering we recommend mTLS for service-to-service; we can support client certs if required.
00:18:39 - Daniel: good. overall we have enough to move forward — we want the documents to review with legal & infra.
00:18:46 - Lena: recap and next steps — Lena sends SOC2 & legal templates; Iris sends BYOK design; Samir schedules tabletop and shares runbook template; Halo shares network diagram.
00:19:00 - 00:48:00 - [Remaining time spent clarifying small points: sample SLA phrasing, fine-grain RBAC roles, export formats for logs, and confirming dates for next tabletop. Multiple short clarifications and micro-decisions recorded in the chat. No substantive objections left. Meeting ended with agreement to reconvene after doc review.]

End of transcript.
